nodes.summary: `I(X; Y | Z) = 0` exactly when `X` and `Y` are conditionally independent given `Z`: `p(x, y, z) p(z) = p(x, z) p(y, z)` for every atom.
nodes.title: Vanishing conditional mutual information iff conditional independence

nodes.summary: `I(X; Y | Z) = H(X, Z) + H(Y, Z) - H(X, Y, Z) - H(Z)`.
nodes.title: Conditional mutual information in terms of entropies

nodes.summary: The conditional mutual information `I(X; Y | Z)` of a finite joint law `p` of `(X, Y, Z)`, in bits: `∑ p(x, y, z) log₂ (p(x, y, z) p(z) / (p(x, z) p(y, z)))`.
nodes.title: Conditional mutual information of a finite joint law

nodes.summary: `I(X; (Y, Z)) = I(X; Z) + I(X; Y | Z)`. Here `p` is read as a joint law of `X` and the pair `(Y, Z)`.
nodes.title: Chain rule for mutual information

nodes.summary: `I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)` for a finite joint law.
nodes.title: Mutual information in terms of entropies

nodes.summary: Data-processing inequality, first half: if `X` and `Z` are conditionally independent given `Y` (a Markov chain `X - Y - Z`, stated as `I(X; Z | Y) = 0` for the joint law `p` of `(X, Y, Z)`), then `I(X; Z) ≤ I(X; Y)`.
nodes.title: Data-processing inequality

nodes.summary: Data-processing inequality, second half: under the same Markov condition, `I(X; Z) ≤ I(Y; Z)`.
nodes.title: Data-processing inequality

nodes.summary: Mutual information `I(X; Y)` of a finite joint law `p` of `(X, Y)`, in bits: the real value of `measureMutualInformation` on `p`, which is finite here (`finiteMutualInformation_eq`). Each finite alphabet carries the discrete σ-algebra.
nodes.title: Mutual information of a finite joint law

nodes.summary: An atom's mass is at most the mass of its image.
nodes.title: Atom mass is at most the mass of its image

nodes.summary: Relabeling the image of a map by a bijection preserves entropy.
nodes.title: Entropy of a pushforward is invariant under relabeling

nodes.summary: Entropy times `log 2` as a `p log p` sum.
nodes.title: Shannon entropy as a p log p sum

nodes.summary: `∑ p(t) log (p.map f)(f t) = -H(p.map f) log 2`.
nodes.title: Log-sum against a pushforward equals its negative entropy

nodes.summary: Summing a function of `f t` against `p` is summing against the pushforward `p.map f`.
nodes.title: Sums against a pushforward of a finite law

nodes.summary: An atom's mass is at most the mass of its image, as real numbers.
nodes.title: Atom mass is at most the mass of its image, in reals

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
